text:
maria: Heads up — noticed the console SLO page showing a p95 jump for /v1/embeddings around 11:03, but the endpoint breakdown lists two different sample_origin labels (router-fallback and client). looks like the high p95 is from a tiny router-fallback cohort (count ~8) while client calls are fine.

sam: ugh that explains why the overall p95 looks bad but our traffic didn't regress. can you paste the tile/query?

maria: here's the query we use in the dashboard:
```
SELECT quantile(0.5)(latency) AS p50, quantile(0.95)(latency) AS p95, quantile(0.99)(latency) AS p99, count() AS sample_count
FROM http_requests
WHERE endpoint = '/v1/embeddings'
GROUP BY sample_origin, endpoint
```
The problem: the default rollup merges sample_origin and we surface only the merged percentiles without showing the small-cohort counts.

jake: can we add a small "confidence" badge next to each percentile that goes dim if sample_count < 100? simplest UX that prevents misreads. :thinking_face:

anya: or show inline sample_count for each percentile slice (p50[pct=125k], p95[pct=12], p99[pct=3]) — very explicit. Also an info tooltip: "percentile computed across merged cohorts; small cohort contributions can dominate tail percentiles".

sam: agreed. also we should annotate when routing policy changed — the spike aligns with the new fallback weighting rollout at 11:00. a timestamped annotation on the chart would make the causality obvious.

maria: +1. devs keep misinterpreting p95 jumps as product regressions when it's a routing artifact. we lose time triaging.

jake: implementation note: on the backend we can compute per-origin quantiles and counts and then compute a merged quantile for display, but keep the per-origin rows accessible. that way the UI can highlight tiny cohorts. pseudocode:
```
for origin in origins:
  q[origin] = quantile(latencies[origin])
  n[origin] = len(latencies[origin])
merged_q = quantile(concat(all latencies))
```
We should avoid approximating merged_q by weighting quantiles by n (wrong).

anya: YES please call out the incorrect weighted-quantile heuristic in the docs. we've seen folks implement WQ = sum(q_i * n_i)/sum(n_i) and it looks plausible but is mathematically incorrect for percentiles.

maria: UX ask: can we add a toggle on the SLO summary to "show per-origin breakdown" and a threshold slider (hide cohorts smaller than N) so product owners can quickly filter noise?

sam: I'll file a small product ticket and link it to the routing rollout PR. can someone propose API changes? we might need an endpoint like /metrics/percentiles?include_origins=true&min_count=10

jake: API: returning a list of rows is easiest: [{"origin":"client","p95":"12ms","count":"12400"}, ...] — simple and consistent with other metric endpoints. keep everything stringified for the console so no surprises.

anya: also propose a visual treatment: tiny cohorts (count < threshold) show with a dashed outline and a hover that says "small sample — treat tail with caution". design will mock up by EOD.

ops-bot: deploybot: routing-adjust 2025-06-18T11:00:00Z deployed to staging (rollout 20%), linked to #routing.

maria: perfect timing — thanks. goal: reduce "false alarm" p95 tickets by surfacing sample_count + origin on the SLO page.

sam: nice. I'll add the annotation and file the API ticket now. tagging @jake and @anya for implementation + design. :thumbsup:

jake: ok I'll carve out time tomorrow to add per-origin quantile fetch and make sure we don't accidentally send approximated weighted quantiles.

anya: will upload mock in the design drive and put link in the ticket.

maria: thanks team — will follow up if we see another spike.
